claim.statement: The dominant cause of a reasoning act ending in Kimera-SWM is the DEATH OF THE OSCILLATOR that drives it. 68.5% of cycles (353/515) end via M2 amplitude_death — the Routh-Hurwitz gate fires when accumulated delay τ exceeds τ_crit = 1/(4ω), debounced. Cognition in this substrate is mortal: gamma-band coherence collapses, the Walker halts, the act ends.
claim.operationalization: Count cycles by halt_reason across the 515-cycle M.46 Shakespeare run. amplitude_death rate is the headline observation. The Routh-Hurwitz mechanism is documented at prime_topology_walker.py:21-22 with literature citation (Reddy/Sen/Johnston 1998).
claim.h0: Cycles end primarily by other means (graph-exhaustion, budget, error)
claim.h1: Cycles end primarily by oscillator collapse (M2 amplitude_death)

preregistration.analysis_plan: Count halt-reason distribution; verify M2 dominance.

verdict.reasoning: 353/515 = 68.5% of cycles end via M2 amplitude_death. Only 28.3% reach graph exhaustion. Only 2.9% hit selective. The oscillator's mortality (Routh-Hurwitz delay accumulation beyond 1/(4ω)) is the dominant architectural cause of cycle end.
